I teach undergraduate and postgraduate courses in applied statistics, spatial statistics, survival analysis and statistical programming. I try to connect theory with practice, and R is central to how I teach.

## Teaching philosophy

I want students to think critically, solve practical problems and understand statistical ideas deeply. My classes combine theory with real-world applications through R, R Shiny apps, live coding and group work, in an environment where every student feels able to take part.

I adapt my approach to each audience. For service courses I simplify concepts without losing depth, I take applied students through both the theory and the software, and I give mathematically strong students harder problems.

Innovations I have introduced include:

- Posit (RStudio) Cloud for real-time feedback on students' scripts during online learning
- R Shiny applications that let students explore statistical concepts without prior coding experience
- A pre-semester R bootcamp (2022) to close gaps left by online learning
- Group R Shiny projects for applied, collaborative learning
- Sentiment analysis of students' written feedback to better understand their learning experience
